unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U22: Classify director-connected loans,conflicts and loss-of-office payments

payload.title: Connected does not mean one universal permission or prohibition
payload.core_explanation_md:
Section185 distinguishes the specified prohibited director/relative/firm transactions from the conditional route for defined interested entities and from stated exceptions. The conditional route includes a special resolution and the borrower principal-business use, with the required explanatory disclosure. The textbook blanket ban followed by a broad subsidiary exemption must not replace these categories. Other provisions and company-class notifications can also apply.

Related-party transactions require their own disclosure, approval and exception analysis; an ordinary business label alone is not proof that every condition is met. Compensation linked to loss of office on the described transfers has disclosure and approval requirements; receipt before or contrary to the required approval can engage the trust consequence. Review both the recipient and the transaction purpose.

self_check.prompt_text: Can subsidiary status alone establish every connected-loan exemption?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The particular exception and its conditions must be established.

payload.stem_md: A director receives transfer-related loss-of-office compensation before the required member approval. Which issue should be examined?

options.explanation_md: Receiving money is a different event from obtaining the prescribed disclosure and member approval.

options.text_md: Whether all compensation is always forbidden
The section 191 disclosure, approval and trust consequence
Whether the director owns a cheque book
options.explanation_md: A personal payment instrument does not establish the required approval for the loss-of-office compensation.
